questions.question: Compare absolute specificity, group specificity, and stereospecificity with suitable examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare absolute specificity, group specificity, and stereo- specificity with suitable examples.
  • Enzyme specificity- introduction ((5 marks)), Absolute specificity-definition- refers to an enzyme acting on one
  • particular substrate , example- urease–urea etc – 1 .(5 marks), group specificity – definition-involves substrates
  • with particular structural features, example-trypsin–peptide bonds after lysine or arginine etc, - (1.5 marks)
  • stereo-specificity- definition- involves recognition of a particular stereoisomer , example- L-amino acid
  • oxidase–L-amino acids etc- (1.5 marks).

questions.question: Classify fumarase based on its catalytic activity and explain the type of reaction it performs.
questions.solution_html:
• Classify fumarase based on its catalytic activity and explain the type of reaction it performs.
  • Lyase class - introduction- (1 mark), explanation- Fumarase is a lyase (EC 4; EC 4.2.1.2) that catalyses the
  • reversible hydration of fumarate to L-malate and dehydration of L-malate to fumarate in the citric acid cycle.
  • Any 4 points- (4 marks).
